headline: DR Congo Demands $6 Million from Chinese Mining Giant CDM Over Wastewater Spill
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's mines ministry stated that Chinese-owned mining company Congo Dongfang International Mining must pay $6 million in compensation to three communities affected by an industrial wastewater spill, despite the company having suspended operations.
why: CDM is a major mining operator in DR Congo, and environmental liabilities and regulatory penalties affect foreign mining investments in the region.

impacts.name: Congo Dongfang International Mining
impacts.why: Fines and suspended operations directly increase legal and operational costs for the mining subsidiary.
